Question: AstraZeneca, a British pharmaceutical giant, has admitted that its Covid-19 vaccine can result in a rare side effect of TTS. Majority of Indians have got this Covishield vaccine and how will it affect Indians?
Answer: We all take Paracetamol. Do you know that an “unintentional” overdose of Paracetamols is the most common cause of acute liver failure in the UK and USA? So, should we stop taking Paracetamol? For the first time AstraZeneca (the company that made the Covishield Vaccine with Oxford University) has accepted that in very very rare cases, the Covishield vaccine can cause a type of blood clotting (a disease called TTS). There have been earlier reports in media that the Covishield can cause TTS but the company has accepted this for the first time. But Covishield is not the only Corona vaccine that has side effects. All other major Corona vaccines like Pfizer, Moderna, Jhonson & Jhonson have known side effects. Covishield is a traditional vaccine but the Pfizer and Moderna vaccine uses the new mRNA technology and many people across the world have accused these mRNA vaccines of many side effects (like fatal heart attacks, deadly heart problems etc). Around 80 to 90 percent of Indians have received Covishield vaccine. The Covishield vaccine was given the go-ahead by almost every country of the world. Covishield was also approved by WHO. India’s Serum Institute was the biggest manufacturer of the Covishield vaccine and India exported these vaccines to over 90 countries. Normally it takes 5 to 10 years to develop a vaccine but the Coronavirus Pandemic was such a big threat to humanity that scientists across the globe created many vaccines within a few months and all Governments gave them emergency usage certificates. Ideally, these vaccines should not have been approved so quickly but it was a race against time. Some people in the world may have died or may have got complicated diseases due to Corona vaccine (cases are going on in courts of Western countries) but these vaccines have saved millions of lives. As per AstraZeneca’s statement in British Court, the company said that their Covishield vaccine saved the lives of 65 million people worldwide. Goverments had to take decision and they chose a path which has saved much more lives. We all remember the horrors of the second wave of the Coronavirus Pandemic when India was brought to its knees by the virus but we were able to take subsequent waves due to Covishield vaccine. The other option for India was the Pfizer mRNA vaccine and later it turned out that this vaccine also had some side effects. Pfizer Vaccine was very costly (Covishield was not patented and its formula was given to India without profit by Oxford University) it needed deep freezers to keep it very cool. India could have afforded the cost of the Pfizer Vaccine but India could not have distributed these vaccines due to lack of deep freezers in remote villages. Almost all of us would have lost many of our family members and friends without Covishield. This has saved the lives of millions of Indians who would have died in 3rd and 4th wave of the pandemic. As per some studies, 2 to 3 lakh people in America have died due to coronavirus due to their refusal to take the vaccine. But at the same time, let’s accept the side effects also. There is not a single drug in the world that has no side effects. And many more Indians die due to “casual” use of antibiotics. If you want to keep your family safe please stop using eating antibiotic tablets in normal circumstances. And most of the side effects of Coronavirus vaccines are seen in the first few days/months of taking the vaccine doses. So, we all are safe and there is no need to panic. If you get blood clotting then consult doctor and take the prescribed medication. As per some reports the side effect has been seen in less than 40 people out of 1.75 cr plus people and the rate of side effect is 0.00000007%. I support the decision of the Modi Govt. and our institutions (like IMCR) to use Covishield in 2021. That was the best decision based on the circumstances. That was a war-like situation and the decision was 100% correct based on all the available information. And, I also the Serum Institute which produced so many vaccines very quickly. Do you know that some people die due to drinking “excess” milk? Do you know that wheat increases the chances of death in some diseases? Do you know that some people have died after eating rice? If you are eating any medicine (or even food) then please go and read the side effects of those on the internet. There are almost 8 billion people on the earth and everything is bad for someone.

Question: Will a low turnout affect the BJP?
Answer: The overall turnout in the 2024 Lok Sabha election is less than that of the 2019 Lok Sabha election. Let us see the turnout of the last 7 Lok Sabha elections - 1991 (56.73%), 1996 (57.94%), 1998 (61.97%), 1999 (59.99%), 2004 (58.07% ), 2009 (58.21%), 2014 (66.44% - highest ever till then), 2019 (67.40% - all-time high). Some states like UP, Bihar, Gujarat, and Rajasthan have seen the highest drop in voting percentage.. On the other hand, some states like J&K, Telangana, Karnataka, Chhattisgarh, etc. have witnessed higher voter turnout in 2024 compared to the last phase. Some states Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, etc. have seen similar voter turnout. The turnout in the 2024 Lok Sabha election has been increasing slowly phase by phase. The Phase 6 election turnout in the 2024 Lok Sabha election is higher than the last time. Let’s take the example of Bihar. The lowest turnout in Bihar is Nawada - 43.1%. Bihar’s lowest turnout was in 1st phase and Nawada was in 1st phase. Bihar’s first two phases witnessed less turnout. One of the reasons for that was that those two days had heavy “lagan” (auspicious day for marriages and other activities etc.). Nawada is a seat that has a sizable general caste population and the election date was the most auspicious day )of the year) for thread ceremony and good day for marriage. Even my family in North Bihar had 4 invitations for marriage and thread ceremony. But after two rounds the voting in Bihar has increased. As per C Voter, there has been no pattern in the relatively “low” turnout in the 2024 election. It’s uniform across all communities/castes/regions. In 2004, there was 18% decrease in urban voter turnout but this has not been seen in 2024. In Bihar, we have seen that voter turnout has been low across all areas. It has been witnessed that the voter turnout had decreased in Muslim-dominated areas also (compared to the last time). It is generally believed that voter turnout in Muslim-dominated areas is greater than in the rest of the areas. Even among poor communities, we have not seen higher voter turnout as voter turnout has been uniform across all castes/communities/groups. If BJP voters have not turned out in greater numbers in some seats of Bihar then anti-BJP voters have also not tuned out in greater numbers in to defeat BJP. Let’s talk about another data - In my native seat of Ujiyarpur (Bihar), Men’s voter turnout was 9% less than that of women. In my neighboring seat of Samastipur, this difference has been 10%. in 4th phase in Bihar, 8% more women voters voted compared to men. There are all indications that on a national level women voters have supported BJP more compared to other parties due to various reasons (despite Rahul Gandhi’s promise to give one lakh rupees to one woman of a poor family). In Bihar and UP, the BJP has the upper hand in women voters and in some states Congress promise has reduced this gap. So, more women’s support for BJP may be the single biggest factor in deciding the outcome of the 2024 Lok Sabha election. This relatively low overall turnout has sent mixed signals for all parties. It can’t be said that it will only hurt the BJP but I think this will hurt all political parties. The leftist liberal media tried to create an impression after 1st phase that the BJP was losing after low turnout. This has galvanized BJP workers and now the turnout has been increasing after each phase. It seems that BJP has the upper hand but we need to wait till June 4th for the result. By the way, we may still see higher voter turnout in 2024 compared to all elections from 1991 to 2009.

Question: Do Hindus eat eggs, milk, meat, fish, etc.?
Answer: Almost all Hindus drink milk and eat milk products (most of Indian sweets are made up of milk). There is hardly any concept of Vegan in Hindus. And a significant portion of Hindus in India eat eggs, meats and fish. This is one survey religion wise which states that 44% of Hindus are vegetarian. Image Source - Pewresearch Now a days more and more Hindus have started to eat egg and meat. The percentage of Vegetarian in younger generation in Hindus is far less compared to middle and and older generation. There are many reasons for this - migration for studies and job, the influx of Western culture, peer pressure etc. But there is a big difference between a non-vegetarian Indian (mostly Hindus) and other non-vegetarian groups (across the world). Indians consume very less quantity of meat and many of them will eat meat once in a week/few days. Very few Hindus/Indians eat meat daily. If you would compare it to Western Europe, America or West Asia, there you find that normally people would eat meat almost every day. And a significant amount of non-vegetarian Hindus don’t eat meat on certain days (Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays etc.) or during religious festivals (like Navaratri, Ganesh Chaturthi etc.). At best Hindus are occasional meat eaters. In many Indian states, caste factors plays an important role in food choices (like vegetarian or non-vegetarian) but in Bihar it has hardly any affect. My family priest is non-veg and I have many non-Brahmin friends who are vegetarian.
